problems: One state only in this batch; nine pages opened (the budget for 27 shapes) and nine cited: English overseas possessions, Thirteen Colonies, Willoughbyland, Province of New York, Rupert's Land, Treaty of Madrid (1670), Treaty of Utrecht, Madras Presidency, Treaty of Saint-Germain-en-Laye (1632). All loaded; none failed.

WebFetch returns a model summary, not the page text: the overseas possessions page (a map-list article with no infobox) came back as a table whose entries are paraphrases, so its notes are written as paraphrases; text in quotation marks is only what the tool itself quoted.

The Cliopatria row is a composite (English possessions 1609-1712, Madras/Bombay/Masulipatnam 1713-1779) and is not a single state: typed colony, family britain, dated 1607-1779 only because the row is; the English phase ends in 1707 (rename event) and the 1713 row split to british-colonial-empire is a confidence-1 bookkeeping event.

Row overlaps for eu-11 (british-colonial-empire, 771 of 777 cells double-drawn in 1709-1712) and sa-06 (british-empire: Madras, Bombay and Masulipatnam in 1762, Bombay 1763-1779, Masulipatnam 1769-1779); the shared Wikidata Q8680 note in the brief does not apply to this row (its id is Q617219).

21 of 28 verdicts are 'adjust': mostly one mechanical correction adding Saint Kitts and Nevis (from 1626) and Montserrat (from 1632), which the overseas possessions page lists and Cliopatria does not draw; the others are the Suriname block (80 cells against 120 km2), Belize overdrawn, the St. Augustine cells, and the 1607 new keyframe.
Gazetteer: the place 'Hudson Bay' is a Saskatchewan town and 'Jamestown' resolves to non-Virginia places; coordinates were used for both.
16 of 62 events are confidence 1 (page silent), recorded so that every shape change has an event; the reviewer should treat them as gaps, not claims.
